editorial:
Imagine coming back to your hometown with nothing but a dream to change people's lives through reading. You get to follow Todri, a teacher who is deeply in love with his country and wants to bring literacy to the Albanian people. It is a slow-burn drama that feels very grounded and sincere. You will see a man fighting an uphill battle against old ways of thinking and people who are scared of change. The vibe is very inspiring, making you feel the weight of every single letter he teaches the locals to write.

What really hits home is the acting, as you can feel Todri's frustration and passion in every scene. While the pacing is a bit slow for some, it helps you feel the struggle of the time period. If you enjoy stories about underdog teachers, you will love this one. Since it is an older TV movie, you might want to look for a restored version to add the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for the best quality. Otherwise, renting it on Apple TV is a great way to check it out without committing too much.
endingExplained: By the end, you see that Todri's hard work finally pays off. The community stops fighting him and starts to embrace education. The final scenes show the locals reading and writing for themselves, proving that knowledge is the best way to move forward. It wraps up on a high note, showing that one person's stubborn belief in education can truly lift an entire village out of darkness and ignorance.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about teachers and overcoming obstacles.
